notes: This contract pins Umbra's opt-in, non-installable embedded temporal-role development slice to source-derived IEEE 1516.1-2025 records. It keeps Enable Time Regulation and Enable Time Constrained pending until their respective standard callback is dispatched; stores the requested lookahead only when time regulation becomes enabled; exposes Query Lookahead; and clears the corresponding mode on Disable. Relevant role state changes re-evaluate the bounded embedded TAR scheduler. The role callback tests use the federate's current time; timestamped callback times and retraction lifetime are covered by separate service contracts. Focused regressions now include default-region and explicit-source regional timestamped interactions plus an explicit-source regional timestamped object update that remain queued across a Time Constrained disable/re-enable cycle, while a separate normal-interaction regression proves that disabling regulation temporarily removes Retract authority without terminalizing a live designator and that callback-gated re-enable at the same lookahead permits one legal Retract before normal terminal classification. The JNI/Java/JPype callback-gating companion exercises the same lifecycle through both HLA_EVOKED and HLA_IMMEDIATE, preserving the pending-request and already-enabled exception mappings. Separate restore-control regressions return a saved actual lookahead after a post-save increase and retain one saved deferred decrease target; they do not establish general time-role save/restore behavior. It does not cover complete TSO delivery/order, asynchronous delivery, the separately traced Modify Lookahead service, full enable-time coordination, broader re-enable matrices, package support, catalog result, JUnit sidecar, protected review, or conformance claim.
